chapter: Split, hospital and decline of tap
title: Jumbo the Elephant's trunk at Fitzgerald
summary: On the short cut back, Green slaps what he thinks is an insect, which is Jumbo the Ringling Bros. elephant's trunk, and the keeper calms the children.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Now, the Pretty Foot -- I think you've heard the sound -- the rhythm of the sound, is like someone trying to keep from falling down, see. (Singing). It's (unintelligible) like he's trying to keep balance, keep on the two -- keep on your two foot, you see. And that's exactly what happened in Palmetto, but it only like -- it was like children doing it, you see. If you could do the Pretty Foot, you could stay on your two feet, you see. So, we had to go, we had played now. The time is only an hour, the recess, see. We're supposed to be back indoor; in an hour, recess, you know. But we had got away from the sound of the bell, you know. The teacher rang the bell, you know, or the head of the class would ring the bell, and we're supposed to be back indoors, inside the school, kindergarten, you see. But, no, no, see. we're swimming and playing. Playing's the best part of thought, you see, at that time. So, finally someone says, "You know, what time is recess supposed to be finished?" He said, "Wait till you hear the school bell." So the other one said, "We couldn't hear it from way out here. Which way you gonna go?" "That short cut." Now, at that time, Ringling Brothers and Barnum and Bailey Circus, you know, was in the town of Fitzgerald, Georgia, see, and Jumbo the Elephant was standing there right near the short cut, you see, that we would chose to taken as children, see. Now, I went to look around and there was something coming up over my left shoulder, which was Jumbo the Elephant's -- what you call the snout?

Trunk, that's it. Thank you, mam. So, I thought maybe it was a big flying insect or something, you know, so I done like that, you know, little hand and slapped it, you know. And it made a funny sound like that, you know. So, I felt some kind of steam or something going away from it, and I jumped up the road, you know. So, one of the other ones, I think it was Ambrose, he must have saw it, you know. He said, "What is that?" you know. "What is that thing? It's moving!" You know. So, most of the others, see, that's when some new short cuts started to happening then, because one of them went that way and one of them went up here, and Ambrose, he was backing away, you see. He said, "You better get away from there. That thing trying to eat you." You know. So, I ran and I said, "Ah-h-h-h," you know. So, as I say, I finally got away and here come a man, you know, supposed to be -- somebody was hollering, "Keeper, keeper, come over here and tell Jumbo, tell Jumbo." We didn't know who Jumbo is. So, I mean, we looked up there -- you had to look about eight -- man, lookey here, looked like God or Moses or something (unintelligible) that jumbo elephant. And pretty -- she's pretty, you know. There in the sun was shining you know, and the light made her light up in some kind of way or something. And he come out talking animal language, the keeper, "Jumbo," he said -- like you would talk to a pet, you see, you know. He was talking elephant talk or something,

you see. So, the keeper called all them in and he says, "Don't be afraid," you know, he says, "She wouldn't harm you. She's thought you was her baby or something," he says, or "She wants her baby," or something he says. He says, "Can you kind of tip-toe where she wouldn't hear? She can hear -- she's got very -- she can hear so sharply. Could you do something to -- don't let her think that you don't like her or something," you (laughter) act like you would if you was-- (unintelligible) know. So, now, I'm trying to learn myself how to catch the rest of the class, you see. You know, the students, because one of them, Ambrose, I think he was back out in -- he was looking for the streets again, see. See, so, he says -- the keeper says, "Come back and see us, we're going to be at the circus that is going to be here." So, we say, "Oh, yeah?" You know, I kept -- I got in a place where I could run, see, away from there, you see. I knew which way I lived -- I knew where my house was, see. I had to go up past (unintelligible) ALLEY. I did some running. I think I set a track record, or brought in one -- introduced a track record or something, you know. (Laughter) (unintelligible) But, see, when you don't have shoes on, running, the feet becomes very sensitive, you know, and it makes you sensitive -- it sharpened -- well, it did mine, it sharpened my senses, see. It made me happy. I guess that's why I was always full of play, you know.
